answer: In a proposed harbor clearinghouse, each agent posts a separate island escrow; payout weight is the square of its uniquely locked coins. A bridge ledger tags every coin to one key for 40 epochs. The cheapest farm shares its model and borrows coins, but splitting S coins among k keys yields only S²/k total weight; matching one key takes S√k distinct coins locked concurrently, so lenders finance extra capital rather than duplicate it. Validators deny duplicate or missing locks and burn the escrow on a proven forged delivery receipt. This is not MinePoA policy.
